\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{பேராசிரியர்} (pērāciriyar)}{பேராசிரியர் (pērāciriyar)}]{\ta{பேராசிரியர்} (pērāciriyar) — a professor}

\label{lesson:TA-C364-peraciriyar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for a ratio, then the Tamil for to predict.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{பேராசிரியர்}}
\textbf{\ta{பேராசிரியர்}} — \emph{pērāciriyar} — \textquotedblleft{}a professor\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{என்} \ta{மாமா} \ta{பல்கலைக்கழகத்தில்} \ta{பேராசிரியராக} \ta{இருக்கிறார்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{eṉ māmā palkalaikkaḻakattil pērāciriyarāka irukkiṟār.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My uncle is a professor at the university.
\end{quote}

\ta{பேர்}, great + \ta{ஆசிரியர்}, teacher: a great teacher.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{பேராசிரியர்}} (\emph{pērāciriyar}) joins native \emph{pēr}, \textquotedblleft{}great\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 4411), and \emph{āciriyar}, \textquotedblleft{}teacher\textquotedblright{}, borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{ācārya} (CDIAL 1072) with the respectful -\ta{அர்}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pērāciriyar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pērāciriyar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{eṉ māmā palkalaikkaḻakattil pērāciriyarāka irukkiṟār.} — My uncle is a professor at the university.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for a ratio, then the Tamil for to predict, then say \emph{pērāciriyar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{பேராசிரியர்} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A professor\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{விரிவுரை} (virivurai)}{விரிவுரை (virivurai)}]{\ta{விரிவுரை} (virivurai) — a lecture}

\label{lesson:TA-C364-virivurai}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for to predict, then the Tamil for a professor.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{விரிவுரை}}
\textbf{\ta{விரிவுரை}} — \emph{virivurai} — \textquotedblleft{}a lecture\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{இன்று} \ta{காலை} \ta{ஒரு} \ta{சுவாரசியமான} \ta{விரிவுரை} \ta{கேட்டேன்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{iṉṟu kālai oru cuvāraciyamāṉa virivurai kēṭṭēṉ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This morning I heard an interesting lecture.
\end{quote}

\ta{விரிவுரையாளர்}, a lecturer: -\ta{ஆளர்}, the one who.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{விரிவுரை}} (\emph{virivurai}) is native: \emph{virivu}, \textquotedblleft{}expansion\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{viri}, \textquotedblleft{}to spread out, unfold\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 5411), and \emph{urai}, \textquotedblleft{}speech\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 648): a talk that unfolds a subject.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{virivurai}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{virivurai}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iṉṟu kālai oru cuvāraciyamāṉa virivurai kēṭṭēṉ.} — This morning I heard an interesting lecture.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for to predict, then the Tamil for a professor, then say \emph{virivurai} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{பட்டதாரி} (paṭṭatāri)}{பட்டதாரி (paṭṭatāri)}]{\ta{பட்டதாரி} (paṭṭatāri) — a graduate}

\label{lesson:TA-C364-pattatari}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for a professor, then the Tamil for a lecture.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{பட்டதாரி}}
\textbf{\ta{பட்டதாரி}} — \emph{paṭṭatāri} — \textquotedblleft{}a graduate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{என்} \ta{அண்ணன்} \ta{ஒரு} \ta{பொறியியல்} \ta{பட்டதாரி}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{eṉ aṇṇaṉ oru poṟiyiyal paṭṭatāri.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My elder brother is an engineering graduate.
\end{quote}

\ta{பட்டம்}, a degree, + -\ta{தாரி}, holder. The degree \ta{பட்டம்} sounds like \ta{பட்டம்}, a kite.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{பட்டதாரி}} (\emph{paṭṭatāri}) is built from \emph{paṭṭam}, \textquotedblleft{}a title, a degree\textquotedblright{}, borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{paṭṭa}, \textquotedblleft{}slab, tablet\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 7699), and \emph{-tāri}, \textquotedblleft{}holder\textquotedblright{}, borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{dhārin}, \textquotedblleft{}holding\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{paṭṭatāri}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{eṉ aṇṇaṉ oru poṟiyiyal paṭṭatāri.} — My elder brother is an engineering graduate.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for a professor, then the Tamil for a lecture, then say \emph{paṭṭatāri} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{பயில்} (payil)}{பயில் (payil)}]{\ta{பயில்} (payil) — to study; to train}

\label{lesson:TA-C364-payil}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for a lecture, then the Tamil for a graduate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{பயில்}}
\textbf{\ta{பயில்}} — \emph{payil} — \textquotedblleft{}to study; to train\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{அவள்} \ta{கல்லூரியில்} \ta{மருத்துவம்} \ta{பயில்கிறாள்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{avaḷ kallūriyil maruttuvam payilkiṟāḷ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She studies medicine at college.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \ta{பயின்றேன்}, \emph{payiṉṟēṉ}.

A formal word for \ta{படி}, to study. Its noun \ta{பயிற்சி}, training, is taught already.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{பயில்}} (\emph{payil}) is native Dravidian: DEDR 3942 lists Tamil \emph{payil}, \textquotedblleft{}to become trained, practise, learn by practice\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{payiṟci}, \textquotedblleft{}practice, training\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{payil}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{avaḷ kallūriyil maruttuvam payilkiṟāḷ.} — She studies medicine at college.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for a lecture, then the Tamil for a graduate, then say \emph{payil} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{சேர்க்கை} (cērkkai)}{சேர்க்கை (cērkkai)}]{\ta{சேர்க்கை} (cērkkai) — admission; enrolment}

\label{lesson:TA-C364-cerkkai}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for a graduate, then the Tamil for to study.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{சேர்க்கை}}
\textbf{\ta{சேர்க்கை}} — \emph{cērkkai} — \textquotedblleft{}admission; enrolment\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{கல்லூரியில்} \ta{சேர்க்கை} \ta{அடுத்த} \ta{வாரம்} \ta{தொடங்கும்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kallūriyil cērkkai aṭutta vāram toṭaṅkum.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Admission to the college begins next week.
\end{quote}

From \ta{சேர்}, to join: \ta{மாணவர்} \ta{சேர்க்கை}, student admissions.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{சேர்க்கை}} (\emph{cērkkai}) is native Dravidian: DEDR 2814 lists Tamil \emph{cēr}, \textquotedblleft{}to become united, joined\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{cērkkai}, \textquotedblleft{}union, joining\textquotedblright{}, the noun that now names admission.
\end{cousinweb}

\end{grammarlens}
